headline: CaramelClient BETA9 - Sign-in, the CurseForge browser and the in-game menu
summary: This release is about the parts that quietly did not work: the Microsoft account the game reads, the CurseForge tab before you searched, and the floating button that opened nothing. Each fix is one small change with a test behind it, and the ones that still need a device are named as such rather than claimed.

items.text: The launcher's exported account now lands in the store the game actually reads, in the game's own base64 alphabet.
The Minecraft services and multiplayer relying parties are minted at sign-in, so a session no longer falls back to a default skin.
The tab lists Bedrock content before you search, in sections: All, Add-ons, Texture packs, Scripts, Worlds and Skins.
Every card shows the project's own CurseForge picture instead of a placeholder.
XAPK and zip packages can be imported from the device, with a progress line while they unpack.
The floating button opens the Mod Menu again: a deliberate press is a tap, not a 200 ms race.
A build without the native menu says so instead of doing nothing.
The button wears a plain three-bar handle rather than the client mark.
The logcat overlay switch takes effect immediately instead of at the next launch.
